name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: Petroline repair continues on its 3-5 week estimate; the Salalah GCC-Iran ministerial remains unrescheduled with no new date. Iraq's PM al-Zaidi now faces his own September deadline to disarm Iran-aligned militias (PMF/Islamic Resistance in Iraq umbrella), a process reportedly facing growing factional resistance, running in parallel with Baghdad's investigation implicating Maysan-based elements of those same networks in the Petroline strike. No further major Hormuz vessel incident this cycle.
importance: Critical — the Hormuz-bypass route, the leading multilateral diplomatic mechanism, and now Iraq's own militia-disarmament credibility are all entangled in the same unresolved attribution question.
assessment: Attribution remains ASSESSED Iran-aligned Iraqi-militia origin, still formally unclaimed. Iraq's parallel disarmament deadline narrows Baghdad's room to maneuver and adds a domestic-sovereignty dimension to a thread previously tracked mainly through Saudi/Omani diplomacy.
lastChange: 2026-09-16 -- Iraq's September militia-disarmament deadline identified as intersecting with the Petroline-attribution investigation; no new reschedule or repair-status data this cycle.
orgRelevance: Continue treating the current disruption level as a multi-week, sustained planning assumption; reassess Gulf-transiting shipping, energy, and insurance exposure accordingly. Watch Iraq's disarmament-deadline outcome as a new near-term indicator alongside Petroline repair progress and any Salalah reschedule.
nextIndicator: A formal attribution statement from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, or Iran; Petroline repair-progress reporting; a rescheduled Salalah date or an unveiled Iran-Oman bilateral shipping arrangement; Iraq's disarmament-deadline outcome; further attacks during the diplomatic gap.

A new attack near Qeshm Island strikes an Iranian commercial vessel (IRIB: 1 killed, 4 injured) and UKMTO reports a separate vessel hit by an unidentified projectile; Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince meets Iranian President Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit in New Delhi — first top-level Iran-UAE contact of the war; Iran's nuclear chief is barred from traveling to the IAEA Vienna conference.

The 14 Sep Salalah ministerial is postponed 'in the interest of consensus'; CNBC publishes satellite imagery confirming the extent of Petroline pipeline damage; a bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane arrangement continues to be advanced separately.

Iraq dismisses the Maysan military commander and provincial police chief after an investigation into the Petroline strikes' Iraqi origin; IRI issues a non-denial; AP reports a 3-5 week repair estimate; the Salalah ministerial collapse is confirmed to stem from a substantive Saudi objection to the Iran-Oman proposal's wording, with no reschedule date set.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's State Council exit-control regulation took effect 15 Sep 2026, authorizing exit bans on citizens whose departure 'may endanger' industrial/technological security in export-controlled sectors (rare earths, batteries, semiconductors) — a lower evidentiary bar than prior rules, with no fixed time limit. This adds a human-capital lever alongside the unchanged military-affiliated license denial (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth. The confirmed 23-25 Sep Xi Jinping Washington visit remains expected to yield a one-year Busan-truce rollover, not rare-earth relief.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output, now deepened by a talent-mobility control instrument that is independent of the summit's likely outcome.
assessment: The chokepoint is deepening structurally (via talent immobilization) even as the diplomatic temperature is set to cool at the 24 Sep summit; even the realistic 'good' summit outcome would not touch either the licensing denial or the new exit-control rule. Supply-chain and technical-talent mitigation should proceed independent of the summit.
lastChange: 2026-09-16 -- China's exit-control regulation on rare-earth/tech engineers took effect 15 Sep, adding a human-capital dimension to the existing licensing chokepoint; no new PRC licensing action this cycle.
orgRelevance: Continue mapping magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities and pursuing second sources without waiting on summit outcomes; separately assess any PRC-based personnel, supplier, or technical-exchange exposure to the new exit-control rule.
nextIndicator: First reported exit-ban enforcement case; any explicit rare-earth licensing signal at or around the 24 Sep summit; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision; any further PRC entity-list action.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: ZNPP remains on stable, restored external power. Trump publicly claimed on 14 Sep that Russia and Ukraine agreed to a mutual energy-infrastructure strike halt; Zelensky disputed the characterization as merely 'a proposal for a mutual halt,' and Ukraine continued striking Russian refining infrastructure (the TANECO refinery, 13-14 Sep) while U.S. diesel prices hit a record ~$6/gallon. Trump separately told Zelensky to stop targeting Russian diesel refineries specifically.
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the energy-strike dispute now also carries direct U.S. domestic fuel-price politics.
assessment: The claimed halt is contested at the head-of-state level rather than confirmed; the prior forecast that it would not hold cleanly is now resolved CORRECT. Domestic U.S. fuel-cost pressure is a new, visible input into the diplomacy.
lastChange: 2026-09-16 -- Trump's claimed mutual energy-strike halt publicly disputed by Zelensky; Ukraine continued refinery strikes; record U.S. diesel price reported.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; treat any reported ceasefire as unconfirmed until both sides jointly affirm it. The expanding deep-strike campaign and fuel-market volatility remain relevant to European energy-security and logistics-cost monitoring.
nextIndicator: A specific, mutually acknowledged grid-infrastructure strike; any formal joint halt announcement with a verification mechanism; further Trump-Zelensky public friction.

name: Space Control / Orbital Weapons Disclosure
status: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink stated in a keynote at the AFA 2026 Air, Space & Cyber Conference (14 Sep) that the Space Force has deployed on-orbit space-control weapons capable of defending the joint force against 'hostile adversary action' -- the first direct U.S. acknowledgment of offensive/defensive weapons in orbit. He declined to specify type (kinetic vs. non-kinetic), scale, or deployment date, and noted the U.S. has tracked Chinese and Russian counter-space development for over a decade.
importance: High — ends a long-standing U.S. policy of deliberate ambiguity on space weapons, reframing space as a domain of open declaratory posture with downstream implications for doctrine, acquisition, and adversary signaling.
assessment: ASSESSED as a deliberate declaratory-posture shift rather than evidence of a new program; the disclosure itself, not the underlying capability, is what changed. Confidence in the broader significance is MODERATE pending further elaboration or adversary response.
lastChange: 2026-09-16 -- thread opened following Meink's on-the-record AFA 2026 disclosure; no further U.S. elaboration or adversary response identified yet.
orgRelevance: Relevant to any space-domain-awareness, counter-space, or resilient-satellite-architecture capability roadmap; no immediate action implied absent further detail.
nextIndicator: Further U.S. official elaboration on capability type, scale, or timeline; Chinese or Russian official response or counter-disclosure; any Golden Dome or Space Force budget language explicitly referencing space-control weapons.
